prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stocks That Could Beat the S&P 500 Over the Next Year

No one can reliably pick stocks that beat the S&P 500. In a typical year most professional fund managers trail the index, and over 15 years about 90% do (per S&P's SPIVA reports). A 10-stock portfolio could beat the index by a lot or lag it by a lot. Treat the list below as a set of ideas to research, not a sure thing.

## Why these stocks
The S&P 500 is already heavily weighted toward mega-cap tech. To beat it, you have to hold something different from it, so this list adds bets on data center power, healthcare and financials.

| # | Stock | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **TSMC (TSM)** | Makes nearly all leading-edge AI chips and can raise prices | Taiwan tensions, tariffs |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips and networking for the largest cloud companies | Relies on a few customers; expensive |
| 3 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Cheaper than peers; Search profits plus Cloud, Gemini and Waymo | AI could erode Search; antitrust rulings |
| 4 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AI demand boosting AWS; retail and ad margins rising | Very heavy AI spending |
| 5 | **Meta (META)** | AI is making its ad targeting better | Large AI spending; Reality Labs losses |
| 6 | **Vertiv (VRT)** | Power and cooling equipment for data centers | Would fall hard if AI spending slows |
| 7 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines and grid equipment as electricity demand surges | Expensive; problems in its wind business |
| 8 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leader in GLP-1 obesity drugs, with a pill version coming | Drug price pressure, competition, expensive |
| 9 | **JPMorgan (JPM)** | Best-run large bank; gains from looser regulation and busier deal-making | Recession or rising loan losses |
| 10 | **Visa (V)** | Earns a fee on a huge share of global card spending; steadier than the rest | Fee regulation, stablecoin competition |

## Things to know before buying
- **Most of these depend on AI spending.** Six of the ten (TSM, AVGO, AMZN, META, VRT, GEV) rise and fall with AI investment. If that spending slows, this portfolio will likely trail the index.
- **My information is dated.** My knowledge runs to about May 2026, so prices, valuations and news may have changed. Check recent earnings and valuations before buying.
- **Measure fairly.** Compare your results with the S&P 500's total return (e.g., SPY including dividends), after trading costs and taxes.
- **Consider a "core-satellite" approach.** For example, keep 70–90% in an S&P 500 index fund and put 10–30% into your picks. You still get the chance to outperform, but a bad year for your picks does much less damage.
- **Equal-weight the positions** (about 10% each) so no single stock decides your year.

This is general information, not personalized financial advice. Your time horizon, taxes and risk tolerance matter a lot. If you tell me more about your situation, such as account type, how much you're investing, or sectors you prefer or want to avoid, I can tailor the list.
